question: Should `meta` become a forward-compatible opaque runtime bag, or should OpenClaw preserve strict canonical runtime config and migrate only named shipped metadata formats through Doctor?
rationale: This is a durable configuration compatibility contract, not a mechanical correctness choice: accepting arbitrary metadata changes what older and newer writers may place in the runtime configuration indefinitely.

options.title: Keep strict runtime metadata
options.body: Reject arbitrary unknown `meta` keys at runtime and add a named doctor migration only when a specific shipped metadata format requires upgrade handling.

options.title: Adopt opaque metadata
options.body: Accept unknown `meta` keys as a supported cross-version contract, document ownership and retention semantics, and add compatibility coverage for config writers and Doctor.

recommendation.title: Keep strict runtime metadata
recommendation.body: Reject arbitrary unknown `meta` keys at runtime and add a named doctor migration only when a specific shipped metadata format requires upgrade handling.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recently merged work is the closest current example of handling config-version compatibility through doctor-owned migration rather than runtime fallback.
